subject: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification (post-call recap)

Hi Sam, thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned on performance targets and VPC connectivity for the Acme POC: 

Summary of customer goals (from call):
- Real-time chat & streaming responses for agent workflows. Expect ~100 concurrent agents at peak.
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency <= 250ms for non-streaming, and token-to-token streaming latency <= 60ms for streaming sessions.
- Sustained throughput target: ~100 requests/sec across the fleet; burst concurrency up to ~300 concurrent open sessions.

Items we need to validate on the network side (thanks for volunteering details on the call):
1) Connectivity approach: will you use AWS VPC Peering between Acme production VPC and Redwood Private (or VPN)? Please confirm exact architecture (peering vs. VPN vs. Transit Gateway).
2) Egress/NAT: any outbound NAT/egress proxies that could apply to traffic to Redwood endpoints? If yes, please share the egress IP ranges we should expect so we can whitelist.
3) Internal latency budgets: please confirm internal app-to-gateway latencies (p50/p95), e.g., app -> NAT -> peering -> Redwood.
4) Network diagram & routing: please attach a simple VPC diagram that shows subnets, route tables, and whether traffic traverses a firewall/inspection layer.
5) MTU/packet-path concerns: let us know if you have tunnel MTU <1500 (common with some VPNs) so we can adjust keepalive and chunk sizes for streaming.

Proposed test plan / next steps:
- You to share network diagram + traceroute from your app host to our private endpoint (simple traceroute and a curl -v) - target by EOD Wed (Dec 9).
- We will run a short A/B test in staging to validate streaming token latency and steady-state throughput. Jordan and Neha will own the test plan and timing.
- We'll document required firewall/NAT allowlist entries once we have the exact egress IPs.

Attaching the initial mutual action plan (MAP) that steps through discovery -> test -> rollout (post-call-MAP.xlsx).

If any of the SLOs above are optimistic from your side, call it out and we'll prioritize adjustments (e.g., lower concurrency, rethink streaming chunking).

Thanks - looking forward to the diagram and traceroute.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: post-call-MAP.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120 KB)

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme_netops@acme.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa - good recap. Quick answers inline below and attached our VPC diagram + a copy of the VPN config for completeness.

High-level architecture:
- We plan to use AWS VPC Peering from Acme-prod VPC (us-east-1) to the Redwood-private VPC in the same region. No Transit Gateway for POC.
- Egress: Our requests originate from private app hosts in the prod subnet. Traffic egresses via a NAT gateway in the public subnet; there is an inspection layer (inline IDS) that could add ~5-15ms. We can schedule a window to bypass inspection for test traffic if needed.
- IPs to whitelist (egress): 198.51.100.12/32 (app hostnat), plus 198.51.100.0/28 (NAT pool).

Observed internal latency today (sample from app to NAT to peer):
- p50: 8ms
- p95: 22ms

Target SLOs - we heard you on the call and are comfortable with initial acceptance criteria of p95 <= 250ms end-to-end. We'll push for <200ms if Redwood's streaming latency is within the 40-60ms range.

Attachments: acme_vpc_diagram.pdf, vpn_config.txt

Let us know a good time for the traceroute - I can run from our prod host and share the output. We're available Thursday morning PST.

Sam Torres
Head of Platform Engineering
Sam.Torres@acme.com
+1 (617) 555-0199

Jordan / Neha - forwarding Sam's response and attachments. Quick internal asks so we can scope the staging test: 

1) Jordan: can you confirm whether our private deployment will accept traffic from their peered CIDR without additional VPN-level translation? If not, what do we need to change on our side for seamless peering?
2) Neha: can you validate the streaming path - specifically, do we have any internal proxy or egress translation that could add >20ms to token-to-token latency? Also confirm if we can disable gRPC keepalive thresholds for the test if the MTU is small.
3) Please review the attached acme_vpc_diagram.pdf and vpn_config.txt they provided.

Proposed internal timeline:
- Fri (Dec 11): engineering reviews + draft test plan.
- Mon (Dec 14): run traceroutes + initial streaming token latency test in staging.

I'll coordinate the test window with Sam once you confirm readiness.

Thanks - Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification (post-call recap)

Sam - thanks for the diagram and the quick answers. We reviewed the attachments and sketched a short test plan to validate the streaming & steady-state throughput. High-level items: 

1) Peering validation: confirmed - VPC peering is fine for the POC. We only need the peered route table entries and your egress CIDR whitelisted on our side (198.51.100.12/32 + 198.51.100.0/28). No VPN translation required for the flows you described.

2) Streaming latency expectations: we expect to be able to meet token-to-token latencies in the 40-70ms range given their reported internal p95 22ms, plus our internal processing. The inline IDS adding 5-15ms is acceptable for POC; if you can bypass for the test window we can likely shave ~10ms off the total.

3) Test plan (short):
- Thursday 2026-12-16 09:00-10:30 PST: run traceroute and curl -v from a representative app host (Sam to run and share).
- Friday 2026-12-17 13:00-15:00 PST: streaming token latency test (3 x 5-minute runs) from their staging host to our staging Private deployment. We'll stream synthetic sessions (50 concurrent streams) and record token latency distributions.
- Post-test: engineering will produce a one-page test report with p50/p95/p99 and recommended configuration (network MTU adjustments, keepalive tuning, any proxy bypass requests).

Attached: network_test_plan.md (test checklist & scripting snippets). Could you confirm Thursday morning for traceroute? If that works we'll provision the staging endpoint and provide an ephemeral host to run the streaming run against.

Thanks - Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Attachment: network_test_plan.md
